headline_marked: NW Bangladesh: [[Groundwater recharge rates plummet]], risking water security
headline: NW Bangladesh: Groundwater recharge rates plummet, risking water security
summary: A study reveals groundwater in seven northwest districts is replenishing far below normal rates, with water levels dropping from 16m to 36m since 1985.
details: A recent study by the Institute of Water Modelling (IWM) warns that groundwater in seven northwest districts of Bangladesh is replenishing at just 100-210mm, far below the normal rate of 100-515mm.
The affected areas include Chapainawabganj, Rajshahi, Naogaon, Joypurhat, and parts of Dinajpur, Natore, and Bogura.
Data from 1985 to 2025 shows a dramatic drop in the water table, with the depth of groundwater increasing from 16 metres to 36 metres over four decades.
Experts warn that if extraction continues to surpass the recharge rate, underground reserves will eventually be exhausted, leading to severe water scarcity.
The crisis is driven largely by uncontrolled private groundwater extraction and a heavy reliance on water-intensive Boro paddy cultivation, which accounts for 91% of Boro irrigation.
To combat this, the IWM recommends bringing private tubewells under a licensing system and shifting from Boro to less water-intensive crops like Aus and Aman rice.
The Ministry of Agriculture noted that while the Barind region produces 42% of the country's rice, the goal is to increase this to 45% through sustainable surface water management.
caption:
Groundwater levels in NW Bangladesh have dropped from 16m to 36m since 1985. The region is facing a critical water security crisis.

A recent study by the Institute of Water Modelling (IWM) warns that groundwater in seven northwest districts of Bangladesh is replenishing at just 100-210mm, far below the normal rate of 100-515mm.

The affected areas include Chapainawabganj, Rajshahi, Naogaon, Joypurhat, and parts of Dinajpur, Natore, and Bogura.

Data from 1985 to 2025 shows a dramatic drop in the water table, with the depth of groundwater increasing from 16 metres to 36 metres over four decades.

Experts warn that if extraction continues to surpass the recharge rate, underground reserves will eventually be exhausted, leading to severe water scarcity.

The crisis is driven largely by uncontrolled private groundwater extraction and a heavy reliance on water-intensive Boro paddy cultivation, which accounts for 91% of Boro irrigation.

To combat this, the IWM recommends bringing private tubewells under a licensing system and shifting from Boro to less water-intensive crops like Aus and Aman rice.

The Ministry of Agriculture noted that while the Barind region produces 42% of the country's rice, the goal is to increase this to 45% through sustainable surface water management.

headline_marked: Bangladesh observes [[state mourning for former Qatari emir]]
headline: Bangladesh observes state mourning for former Qatari emir
summary: National flags fly at half-mast across all government and educational institutions and Bangladeshi missions abroad to honor the late Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani.
details: Bangladesh is observing a day of state mourning on Wednesday, July 15, following the death of the former Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani.

As part of the mourning, the national flag is being flown at half-mast at all government, semi-government, autonomous institutions, educational institutions, and Bangladeshi diplomatic missions abroad.
According to a notification signed by Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani on Tuesday, all entertainment programs across the country have been suspended for the day.
Special prayers are being held in all mosques and other religious places of worship to pray for the departed soul of the former Qatari leader.
The National Parliament of Bangladesh had previously adopted a condolence motion regarding the death of Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani.
caption:
Bangladesh observes state mourning today for the former Emir of Qatar.

Bangladesh is observing a day of state mourning on Wednesday, July 15, following the death of the former Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani.

As part of the mourning, the national flag is being flown at half-mast at all government, semi-government, autonomous institutions, educational institutions, and Bangladeshi diplomatic missions abroad.

According to a notification signed by Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani on Tuesday, all entertainment programs across the country have been suspended for the day.

Special prayers are being held in all mosques and other religious places of worship to pray for the departed soul of the former Qatari leader.

The National Parliament of Bangladesh had previously adopted a condolence motion regarding the death of Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV
